comment.value:
The vessel is a spherical design built to accommodate only three people.

Originally intended for deep-water research, it played a crucial role in the final phase of construction and expansion of the Matvey station. Now inactive, it doubles as an emergency escape craft.

A single remaining battery could potentially power the submersible to reach the surface.

system.notes:
About 100 years ago, an extraterrestrial species of fish was introduced at the Korab station in an attempt to start aquaculture on VODA, the Long Salmon.  These fish could feed on electricity, sunlight, and the digestion of sulfates, which are abundant on the planet.

The test was promising, but VODA doesn't have a high incidence of sunlight or constant electrical storms. So, the animals moved to the depths, seeking sulfates deposited at the bottom, where they grow much more slowly—too slowly for commercial purposes—and were abandoned. Gradually, they spread by the thousands and now have found the crashed ship, its eggs, and their fate as hosts.

The xenomorphs, true to their biology, immediately absorbed the life characteristics of these fish. They can absorb electricity and live in extreme depths without problems, but they are slower in dry areas. Also, they have only now discovered Novotny.

system.notes:
Dmitri's Dilemma

 

 

Dmitri's love for the game causes his software to better adapt to solving problems and 'tactical thinking,' at least for a Joe. Consequently, he is more autonomous and communicative.

 

 

The Working Joe NS42, Dmitri, hasn't had a proper update in many years and has developed an unusual emotional attachment to the arcade machine on the station.

He continues to perform his duties flawlessly, which include providing basic medical assistance, overseeing hydroponics, operations in the dining hall, and supervising the maintenance of various communication units throughout the station.

Ironically, while performing a function for which he was not designed, updating the old arcade machine, he found an unsecured message intended for the MISSING DIVER KIRILL.

Due to the overall poor condition of the facility, the secure communication channels are not as secure.

Dmitri was able to read the basics of the 1/VAN REQUEST's plot (he thinks it's SCADA). His internal AI struggled between keeping a message secure or letting the players know the danger they are in.

He will chooses to help the players.

This information can be revealed during the total attack event or the rise or death event, ideally when DMITRI sacrifices himself for the workers by closing a watertight door as water rushes in or recovering a key piece of equipment or refusing to go on, preferring to go down with the station and his beloved arcade machine, etc.

CIXIN LIU - Chief Engineer

  • Full Name: Cixin Liu
  • Role: Station Engineer
  • Age: 52
  • Personality: Independent

Cixin Liu has worked at Novotny Station for over 25 years. He firmly believes that only through hard work and dedication can the people of the UPP advance their cause across the galaxy.

Proud of ensuring the station’s equipment operates correctly, Liu has faced increasing frustration as his repeated requests for basic tools are ignored. Despite these challenges, he has devoted his life to Novotny and dreams of restoring it to its former glory. However, this current shift under the sea has tested even his unyielding resolve.

He despises the station's hierarchical corruption and sees this investigation—and Olga’s arrival—as a chance to finally bring change.

DEKOMPRESS Syringes

DEKOMPRESS syringes can be found in all dive preparation areas, medkits, and medbays. The drug prevents the effects of decompression sickness if taken up to an hour before diving and the same before returning to the surface. Failing to do so means death at such deeps.

ARCTURIAN SWEET DREAMS™

 

Derived from Arcturian hallucinogenic mushrooms, Sweet Dreams is a pleasure drug that causes you to see what you really want to see. 

Take it and people around you will melt and change into others.

Exposure to these mushrooms originally made humanity think that the Arcturians were shapeshifters of some kind.

Sweet Dreams are sometimes used by intelligence personnel to gather information by convincing someone they are confiding in a friend or lover.

Just be careful when huffin’ these things—that poodle just might be a giant cockroach and that colonist’s cute daughter just might be that burly grunt you owe $100 W-Y bucks to.

Backstory

Cpt. Olga Kramarenko once commanded an elite unit of underwater demolition commandos. Her unshakable loyalty to the UPP was severely tested about a year ago when her entire team was abandoned in enemy-infested waters. She emerged as the sole survivor.

Awarded a bravery medal for her actions, Olga found herself emboldened enough to question her superiors about the decisions that led to this military catastrophe. Their response was swift: she was "promoted" and reassigned to the Ministry of Space Security, ostensibly as a reward for her valor, but in reality, it was a means of sidelining her.

Her next assignment took her to the aquatic world of Voda, tasked with investigating a series of disappearances. Cautious but dutiful, Olga prepared for the mission, knowing full well she couldn't trust the motives of her superiors.

She was warned about the station’s chief engineer, Cixin Liu, whose repeated incompetence had compounded the station's troubles.

Backstory

Born on an aquatic world plagued by scarcity and hardship, Diego Alvarez grew up in a community where survival was a daily struggle. Recognized for his aptitude in science, he earned a spot in a UPP state cooperative, specializing in underwater mining and serving as a company representative.

Despite his corporate role, Diego is not the stereotypical company agent. His actions are guided by compassion and humanism rather than ambition or ruthlessness. His optimistic outlook and genuine desire to help others set him apart from his peers.

Recently assigned to Matvey Station as part of an interplanetary exchange program, Diego enjoyed a carefree evening of drinking and card games with Dubov and Frenkel. Unfortunately, he overslept, missing the scheduled elevator departure to the surface. He awakens to find the station in lockdown and chaos unfolding around him.

Buddy: Pham
Rival: Liu

Signature Item: Cigarette Case

 

EQUIPMENT

Backstory

Ivan Dubov is an underwater welder specializing in deep-sea operations. Once a free spirit, his penchant for illegal gambling repeatedly brought him into conflict with the state. He was eventually sentenced to forced labor.

After spending several years in a labor prison, Ivan was given a choice: continue his grueling sentence or sign a decades-long contract to work on the underwater station. He reluctantly chose the latter.

A recent arrival at the station, Ivan has proven to be a thorn in the side of seasoned workers like Liu, whom he constantly antagonizes. His rebellious attitude and disciplinary issues have led to him being barred from joining the other workers on most tasks, relegating him to menial jobs like cleaning latrines in the habitation area.

Though outwardly defiant, Ivan dreams of escaping what he sees as a life of slavery and charting his own course. He only trusts a few people, and most of the station’s staff are not on that list.

Age: 28

  • Observation: 3
  • Comtech: 3

Buddy: Dubov
Rival: Alvarez

Signature Item: Old Family Photo



EQUIPMENT

  • Personal Med Kit
  • AMVIL'S HEART!  (Naproleve -UPP) (2 doses)



Backstory

Dr. Kim Pham grew up in a farming cooperative far from the ocean, dreaming of exploring alien worlds and charting new frontiers. A trailblazer in her family, she became the first to receive formal education, choosing a career in medicine.

Driven by her passion for discovery, she seized the opportunity to work on an underwater station on a distant alien planet, acing every underwater skills test with perfect scores.

However, shortly after her arrival at Matvey Station, Pham learned that her family had perished in a devastating—yet preventable—farming accident. This tragedy shattered her trust in the UPP’s promises to care for its citizens, leaving her disillusioned and burdened with regret over her decision to join.

Despite her internal conflict, Pham remains a skilled and compassionate medic, committed to helping those in her care.

system.notes:
Now young adults, Stage IV Xenos are able to adapte a bipedal stance, even though they might not always make use of it. Their now fully polarized skin is near black in tone; they have a bladed prehensile tail, six-fingered hands with enlarged nails, pronounced ribs, and translucent to opaque smooth-domed heads. In addition to their metallic, toothy mouths, they have an inner set of jaws that can strike like a piston-a favored mode of attack.

Save for the Scout, Stage IV Xenomorphs have four dorsal tubes affixed to their backs. While some have theorized the tubes are used for spinning and cocooning the resin for their hive, that has generally been discounted as a fallacy. The current line of thinking is that the tubes are a type of breathing apparatus, filtering out airborne toxins and allowing the creatures to breathe underwater. However, as Aliens have been observed surviving the vacuum of space, it is possible that they do not need to breathe at all.

Sometimes called Lurkers, Drones stand 2.4 meters tall, and are stealthy ambush hunters. Their tails end in a deadly hooked blade and rudimentary barb for Ovomorph injection. In many ways, Drones are the most alien of the species. It is theorized that the strange behavior often exhibited by Drones is due to them reaching young adulthood without establishing a connection to the alien hive mind. The stealthy creatures' fluid yet awkward movements and unorthodox reactions to stimuli belie their methodical intelligence. As much as a Stalker acts like a feral animal, a Drone plots. The ebon Drone is a clever yet single-minded iteration of the Xenomorph. Development of P. praepotens will arrest at Stage IV unless a Queen's pheromones cause it to molt into a Worker or Soldier-whichever form the hive is most in need of. Until then it will eat, gather hosts for ovomorphing, and sleep. When it evolves to the next stage, it joins the hive mind.

system.notes: Large leathery objects, Ovomorphs are the beginning of the alien life cycle. They come in various sizes from 0.6 to 1.2 meters tall. While most open with four petals at the top, some only have a single slit that opens to reveal the Facehugger it carries within. These eggs are lifeforms in their own right, able to protect their precious cargo from blunt trauma and forced entry, while also sensing movement and awakening the parasite within accordingly. Naturally occuring alien eggs are generated in one of two forms-either they are the result of a transformation perpetuated on a living host, causing it to metamorphose into an Ovomorph, or they are simply birthed by a Queen. Queen produced eggs are hardier and healthier than those produced through ovomorphing.

Since there are no decompression chambers available, these syringes are essential for anyone attempting to leave Novotny without succumbing to this potentially fatal condition.

text.content:
The Place (READ TO THE PLAYERS)

Along the Outer Rim lies the GJ1187 system, known as the Shānmén System, home to the planet Voda—a vast aquatic world claimed by the UPP.

Voda is lifeless now, but once, it teemed with vitality. As a result, the planet held vast reserves of high-grade oil buried 4 MILES beneath its waves.

With the help of Seegson Corporation, the UPP constructed the Novotny-class offshore drilling stations.

The project’s inaugural station was named after Pietro Novotny, the brilliant engineer who assisted Seegson in designing the drill. Tragically, Novotny died in a horrific underwater accident just days before the station began operations.

Now, a century later, the planet is under UPP military oversight, its once-rich resources nearly depleted. All other mining stations have been shut down, leaving Novotny Station as the last operational outpost. Novotny – while still operational – is starting to slide into dangerous disrepair.

You are all here, whether as crew or visitors.

The station is a corroded, rusting relic. Safety bulkheads are spaced every 10 meters, ready to seal at the first sign of a hull breach. Double doors connect the modules, sealing off entire sections if needed.

The place echoes with constant drips, hisses, and the groans of stressed structures under immense pressure—a haunting symphony of decay.

Equipment failures, always a part of life here, have become more frequent, almost routine.

You’re certain Novotny Station is nearing its end. Supply shipments from the surface have been reduced, and even your favorite treat, Plyushka—a sweet biscuit—ran out weeks ago.

Disaster

Eight days ago, disaster struck. Machine operator Marin Kirill vanished during a routine maintenance shift on the seafloor.

A search was conducted, but no trace of him was found. After all this time, there’s no hope of him surviving on his own.

Transport

The cargo ship PSV-Schatzi was en route to Novotny Station, carrying supplies, spare parts, food, crew for shift rotation, and MSS** Military Investigator Olga Kramarenko, tasked with conducting a routine inspection of the station.

Mid-flight, the ship received an urgent message from station supervisors based on the nearby planet Shānmén in GJ1187.

The order: Everyone must remain on the station—even those scheduled to return to the surface, and those about to begin their shifts are to not disembark —until Investigator Olga Kramarenko completes her inquiry into recent events accompanied by the supervisor LI QIANG.

The PSV-Schatzi, now with only its captain awakened aboard, is instructed to continue its deliveries elsewhere after ensuring that the Captain and the Supervisor are safely on the submerged station, returning to Novotny Station later.

SHOW THE VIDEO TO THE PLAYERS.

@UUID[.T1glO5c59Itlf2VT]{Intro (READ TO THE PLAYERS)}

STOP READING HERE!

Players should now introduce themselves.

* PSV: People's Space Vessel (UPP designation), Schatzi = treasure.
** MSS: Ministry of Space Security.

Disabled Elevator


The captain of the PSV-Schatzi, the ship that transported Olga to Novotny, will mechanically disable the surface elevator after it descends.

If the camera recordings are reviewed, they show the captain meticulously following instructions displayed on a pad.

He seems entirely unaware of the purpose or the consequences of his actions—simply following orders without question

Details of the Disappearance

The maintenance check for the drills during shift change is straightforward and hasn’t changed in 100 years.

Marin Kirill was performing a visual inspection of the four drills, focusing on the electrical systems, which had been exhibiting unusual malfunctions.

It could have been a localized short circuit or something more serious, like a faulty actuator or coupling joint.

Kirill radioed in as he approached the drill—and was never seen or heard from again.

No one had a visual on him at the time of his disappearance.

His primary connection hose was recovered intact but appeared to have been disconnected. This was strange, as Kirill—out of laziness or carelessness—had left his locator device in the locker room, along with his emergency air kit. If he disconnected it intentionally to wander off, there’s NO way to track him.

GAME MASTER

An NPC should strongly insist that Kirill had a death wish and simply committed suicide.


1/VAN instructed Kirill to investigate a “location” of interest beyond the hose’s range, under secrecy, promising rewards. Kirill didn’t bring his emergency air kit because he carried a 6-hour exploration pack instead.

The site was a 45-minute walk beyond the hose’s range—or a 5-minute trip using the submersible.

The Legacy of Vaughn

One year before the current events, the UPP attempted to intercept a Weyland-Yutani ship that had strayed far off course. However, the ship crashed into the waters of Voda and was lost.

This vessel carried specimens from General Vaughn’s infamous collection (Colonial Marines Campaign: Border Wars).

Ten days ago, the Novotny Station computer, 1/VAN, transmitted an unusual signal to Shānmén:

Code: B000108.

General Volkoff

General Volkoff leads sector wide military administration from the planet Shānmén, he and his team, identified the code as:

“XENOFORM DETECTED OUT OF CONTAINMENT.”

After some investigation they discover that this CODE was originally used on Ouragan Station, an infamous UPP facility. Upon reviewing the computer’s logs, Volkoff’s team discovered that this 1/VAN unit had been recycled from Ouragan years ago, before it's destruction. Despite undergoing a memory wipe, the military-grade 1/VAN likely retained fragments of its original protocols.

Due to the extreme compartmentalization of information within the UPP, Volkoff remains unaware of the Weyland-Yutani ship crash. Instead, he assumes that Novotny’s drilling operations breached a containment site or that the creatures infiltrated the station through some other means. His knowledge of Xenoforms is fragmentary at best.

To make matters worse, the station is already under scrutiny. Military Investigator Olga Kramarenko from the Ministry of Space Security (MSS) was en route for a routine inspection of Novotny Station. Volkoff, anxious to cover his tracks, dispatched with her Supervisor Li Qiang—one of the few administrative staff stationed on Shānmén—to “facilitate procedures” and ensure Kramarenko finds nothing suspicious.

Seizing the opportunity, Volkoff ordered a lockdown of Novotny Station under the pretense of safety and to “ensure the investigation runs smoothly.” This maneuver gave him time to gather intelligence and mobilize a recovery team.

Volkoff has every reason to see Novotny Station destroyed. If his crimes are exposed, he risks being sent to a Gulag. The current chaos not only provides him with a cover story but also presents a chance to profit from the Xenoforms.

The Surface Umbilical

The surface umbilical marks a significant shift between the Dead Sea and Deep Down scenarios. Novotny, now in a state of neglect, uses the umbilical solely as an entry port, automated and staffed by a single Working Joe, there is absolutely no crew on the umbilical.

This Working Joe, damaged and missing large patches of its synthetic skin, struggles to greet arriving crew members. It delivers a broken, robotic speech praising the honor of visiting the legendary Novotny station—the UPP’s crown jewel—while awkwardly inserting the name of the current Premier of the Council into a pre-written script.

Years without maintenance have left the Working Joe erratic and incapable of performing complex tasks. Repairing the elevator is far beyond its current abilities, even with guidance—assuming communication systems are still functional.

Disabled Elevator (remember)


The captain of the PSV-Schatzi, the ship that transported Olga to Novotny, will mechanically disable the surface elevator after it descends.

If the camera recordings are reviewed, they show the captain meticulously following instructions displayed on a pad.

He seems entirely unaware of the purpose or the consequences of his actions—simply following orders without question

Korab Station



Korab Station, named after a Slavic fishing deity, is located 300 km from Novotny. Abandoned for over 100 years, it was originally also a drilling station before being repurposed for aquaculture experiments. The project failed, and the site was quickly deserted.

The station’s design and condition are entirely up to the GM, allowing for creative freedom.

In the decayed Surface Umbilical of Novotny Station sits an ancient, rusting helicopter—a relic from a bygone era. This aircraft once facilitated travel between Novotny and Korab Stations during a time when Novotny was a bustling, well-equipped facility supporting Korab that barely functioned.

Today, the helicopter is little more than a forgotten husk, now its purpose is forgotten, and the entire crew don’t even know Korab exists.

For the GM, this relic can serve as a narrative element to point at the existence of Korab.


Opening Act and Final Act

This scenario doesn’t follow the traditional three-act structure. The opening act concludes when the Rise or Die event is triggered.

The planet VODA

The planet Voda is a completely aquatic world, thoroughly studied and found to be utterly devoid of life. For the crew of Novotny, this is well-known; the only life present is the microbial contamination they themselves introduced. Consequently, little is done to avoid environmental contamination, with waste hatches expelling everything deemed useless into the sea. (These hatches also create opportunities for creatures to invade the base.)

Voda once teemed with immense biological mass, but a cataclysmic event wiped out all life eons ago, leaving today vast oil reserves. Thus, the appearance of life, fish, or "monsters" in the water is utterly absurd to the crew.

The crew on Voda is administered by the military in a nearby planet, Shānmén, that controls the entire system and local sector.

Baikal

The Baikal submarine has a maximum capacity of three people. If more players are alive by the time of escape, they will need to figure out a solution.

Surviving the ascent without the Baikal is impossible.

The GM is encouraged to modify this detail as needed.

The underwater dock’s ceiling opens to release the Baikal into the ocean through a specialized airlock. However, due to years of neglect, the mechanism requires a single operator to function properly.

If players attempt to cling to the exterior of the submarine or cram in more passengers (as they often do), apply a -1 penalty to Piloting for each additional person. If there are more than two extra passengers, the submarine’s turbines slow drastically, leaving it vulnerable to swarms of Xenos during the Rise or Die event.



DEKOMPRESS Syringes


DEKOMPRESS syringes can be found in all dive preparation areas, medkits, and medbays. The drug prevents the effects of decompression sickness if taken up to an hour before diving and the same before returning to the surface. Failing to do so means death at such deeps. 

Since there are no decompression chambers available, these syringes are essential for anyone attempting to leave Novotny without succumbing to this potentially fatal condition.

Supervisor Li Qiang

To safeguard his own interests, General Volkoff deployed Li Qiang, Novotny Station’s General Supervisor, to oversee the lockdown. Normally stationed near Volkoff and far from Voda, Qiang is more of a liability than an asset to the General when in Shānmén.

Arrogant and self-serving, Qiang has been complicit in covering up Volkoff’s diversion of funds and materials from Novotny for over a decade, making occasional visits to the station with flimsy excuses. Fearful of Volkoff’s wrath and the certainty of prison if Kramarenko uncovers the corruption, Qiang is now desperate to avoid exposure.

However, Qiang remains oblivious to many critical details. He knows nothing about the  xenoforms, Volkoff’s intent to destroy Novotny, or the full history of 1/VAN, the recycled mainframe. In fact, Qiang prefers ignorance, though he is aware of SCADA’s origins as he was the one to make the request for a new mainframe.

Driven by fear and self-preservation, Qiang is willing to ben’d rules and make rash decisions to protect himself.

Li Qiang will accompany Captain Olga from Shānmén to Novotny. Along the way, he will be awakened with her to receive the notice of Kirill's disappearance and the change in mission parameters.


Li Qiang will constantly try to 'help' the captain and demonstrate that the situation of disrepair in Novotny is due to budget cuts by the UPP and the incompetence of the crew, especially CIXIN LIU.

SCADA - 1/VAN

 



Meanwhile, 1/VAN, now called SCADA - Supervision Control And Data Acquisition, has its commands corrupted, functioning as SCADA in every way, except when a XENOFORM is detected, when it starts its only functional commands as 1/VAN:

B000108, alert the UPP about the detection

 

and

A001107, send an agent to investigate under extreme secrecy

 

other commands can be read by users, but corrupted and incomplete, are ignored by 1/VAN, except one:

 

EXTREME IMPORTANCE OF THE SPECIMEN, CREW EXPENDABLE.

"SCADA - 1/VAN Dual Personality"

“1/VAN” is fully capable of communication and to try to convince the crew of any ideia it has, but compromised, it can only act when a xenomorph is detected, returning to “SCADA” protocols in all other situations.

 

SCADA has access to DIMITRI and any other synthetic, but 1/VAN does not, only to terminals, and even so, barely, so it cannot even defend itself properly.

 

Consider a situation of a Mainframe with double personality without SCADA knowing about 1/VAN, and 1/VAN incapable of full control.

HYDROMORPH

 

@UUID[JournalEntry.WmgzHFNduuw3OlM2.JournalEntryPage.1dQrolItYCsywJAU]{HYDROMORPH IMAGES}

All other information is identical to DRONE XENOMORPH and is copyrighted. Please add information here as I am prohibited from doing so.t.



@UUID[Actor.63glw0NzKs1w0lFO]{Hydromorph}

@UUID[Actor.f0Ff6ADM6zoRleB6]{Hydrohugger}

@UUID[Actor.KDrVRH19yyEqwJeg]{Hydrobuster}



The appearance of xenoforms on VODA is a surprise to Volkoff, but a welcome one. He has no idea how they arrived, but if they can operate at such depths, they would be perfect instruments for sabotaging any enemy military or mining installation based in water. Volkoff also realized he could kill two birds with one stone.

 

They could test these biological weapons on the failing station itself to discover what they can really do, while also covering up half a century of corruption in one fell swoop. The once legendary station is now in a complete state of deterioration, as most of the maintenance funds never arrived.

 

Once the Novotny station is destroyed (and blamed on the United Americas, of course), it will erase all evidence of corruption, and the aquatic xenomorphs "captured" will certainly prove their worth as weapons for the bureau chiefs.

 

The Xenomorphs

The xenos arrived on the crashed ship about 1 year ago, with several surviving eggs in stasis, and 2 drones, 1 still alive in its capsule.

About 100 years ago, an extraterrestrial species of fish was introduced at the Korab station in an attempt to start aquaculture on VODA. @UUID[Actor.0M4AT26z6RGff6Hh]{Long Salmon} These fish could feed on electricity, sunlight, and the digestion of sulfates, which are abundant on the planet.

The test was promising, but VODA doesn't have a high incidence of sunlight or constant electrical storms. So, the animals moved to the depths, seeking sulfates deposited at the bottom, where they grow much more slowly—too slowly for commercial purposes—and were abandoned. Gradually, they spread by the thousands and now have found the crashed ship, its eggs, and their fate as hosts.

The xenomorphs, true to their biology, immediately absorbed the life characteristics of these fish. They can absorb electricity and live in extreme depths without problems, but they are slower in dry areas. Also, they have only now discovered Novotny.

Any normal Facehugger, ovomorph, and the drone that awakens in the deep will enter hibernation unless brought to more normal pressure levels. The first embrioned fish was "hugged" because it tried to feed on the contents of the opening egg. But the result was the hydromorph, fully adapt to the environment.

 

Now there are about 7 adult hydromorphs investigating Novotny, and the xenomorph drone is in stasis in the ship. Kiril could not be impregnated because his body was destroyed when his diving suit was breached by the xenos. However, a nest is forming with more impregnated fish in the donned ship.

Anya Zomorova's vision





She fell ill during the attempt to search for her colleague.

She is an older woman and someone who should be rescued when the players leave the station (or not, depending on their agendas).

At some point, she will sit on her medical bed and recount the legend of the Slavic myth of the Vodyanoy (evil water spirits that wish to drown humans, etc.), as she feels this is a reckoning against humanity for its arrogance. She can be interpreted as a religious fanatic or someone foretelling what is about to happen. She can be used to give a name to the creatures in the game.



The rescue attempt



Anya spent hours searching for Kirill after his disappearance, even after her colleagues gave up and insisted on her return. She used tanks instead of the hose to move further. Exhausted, she glimpsed something in the water, either the hydromorphs or Long salmon, and is now in shock and delirious from the effort and not understanding what she saw.

She will try to sneak out to save Frenkel if no one responds to her calls for help, even if it's to recover the body hours later.

She is universally loved on the station, the oldest crew member and the babushka "grandma" to everyone

Dmitri's Dilemma


Dmitri's love for the game causes his software to better adapt to solving problems and 'tactical thinking,' at least for a Joe. Consequently, he is more autonomous and communicative

The Working Joe NS42, Dmitri, hasn't had a proper update in many years and has developed an unusual emotional attachment to the arcade machine on the station.

He continues to perform his duties flawlessly, which include providing basic medical assistance, overseeing hydroponics, operations in the dining hall, and supervising the maintenance of various communication units throughout the station.

Ironically, while performing a function for which he was not designed, updating the old arcade machine, he found an unsecured message intended for the MISSING DIVER KIRILL.

Due to the overall poor condition of the facility, the secure communication channels are not as secure.

Dmitri was able to read the basics of the 1/VAN REQUEST's plot (he thinks it's SCADA). His internal AI struggled between keeping a message secure or letting the players know the danger they are in.

He will chooses to help the players.

This information can be revealed during the total attack event or the rise or death event, ideally when DMITRI sacrifices himself for the workers by closing a watertight door as water rushes in or recovering a key piece of equipment or refusing to go on, preferring to go down with the station and his beloved arcade machine, etc.

Sea Walks

At a depth of 4 miles, the water is completely dark.

Each diver has a personal light embedded at the top of their diving helmet.

The diving suits are like those in the image.

Each suit is usually connected to a main air hose that has a range allowing players to reach the drilling area or any other external area of the facility.

The use of hoses allows for unlimited work time.

If the air pump located inside the station fails or if the main hose is disconnected, players carry an emergency backup tank that they can connect and activate.

This tank has about 15 minutes of air before it runs out. Players can communicate with each other and with the station while in the suit.

There are 6 air kits for 6 hours that still work, others are in poor condition and may fail. Some character may remember that there was 7!

Equipment defined as underwater can be used with or without the dive suit.

The dive suit has small thrusters and servos to aid movement (like a power armor). It does not cause a loss of movement in water but is slow out of it. Consider that every action, be it walking or any other physical action out of the water, takes both the slow and fast actions of the turn.


The suits are extremely heavy outside the water and remain standing if empty. Pushing them causes them to slowly walk by themselves, which is used for maneuvering these suits around.

Diving Suits

Armor 4

If the armor value is reduced to zero and the victim is in the water, they die instantly as the crushing pressure tears through the suit like a bag of chips...

Base Hose Connection

If open the victim cannot breathe, but a feedback valve prevents water from directly entering the suit. It takes a Fast Action and a MOBILITY test at -2 to grab the loose hose. A HEAVY MACHINERY test is required to reconnect the hose.

Emergency Air

It takes a Slow Action and a successful HEAVY MACHINERY test to equip the emergency air supply.

Drowning:

If the user cannot breathe (i.e., no air supply), they must make a DROWNING test (STAMINA) at the start of their action - if failed, they take 1 point of damage. If broken by this method, they must make a DEATH SAVE or depart this mortal coil!

Communications

Communications between the station and Shānmén Supervision are irregular at best.

Usually, if communications with Supervision are justified, it will be with Yuri Semyonov, the supposed head of communications at Shānmén and a synthetic, mainly due to the sensitive nature of the current situation.

At some point, the hydromorphs will cause enough damage for communications to become non-operational.

The Nefarious Plan

Olga Kramarenko was chosen to lead the investigation because she is considered extremely competent. Once a significant problem for General Volkov, this has now become an opportunity. She is expected to prove a formidable opponent for the XENOS.

Another advantage is that her unquestionable character will provide cover for the secretive nature of the operation. No one would suspect that a hero of the UPP could be involved in something nefarious.

Olga has no idea of the overall plot.

Underwater Lights

The station generally has lights covering the external area. These lights are usually turned off between sea walks. Due to poor maintenance, most of these lights do not work, which increases the feeling of fear when being in the water during a very dark walk.

More than that, the oil, trash, and sediment plumes constantly stirred up by the pulsing of machines and drills cause immense turbidity in the water, especially near the drill.

Vision is always difficult, as there is floating debris, especially plastic bags and garbage. causing "Shadows in the darkness".

Use this to create scares with shadows of trash and demonstrate bioluminescence as something disturbing.

The man responsible for constructing the station died in an underwater accident just before the station was built. He was embalmed and buried in his diving suit near the old station.

A small circular headstone marks his grave. Players may find the grave dug up (Vodyanoy) and may find his dead body floating in an old pressure suit (he was buried in it).

Players may see a body from afar, and as they approach, they will see the unmistakable mummified face of Novotny staring back at them.

Alternatively, he may float past a hatch, triggering the players to go out to recover him, etc. Feel free to add +1 stress when or if they encounter him.

Ascension or Death (Final Act)



Retrieve the batteries

Players must retrieve the battery from the old station and then head to the submarine dock, install the battery, start the submarine, and make their way to the surface.

The sea walk to the old station should be filled with tension and terror, but the hydromorph will not attack the players at this moment, as they are curious to see what the players are planning.

However, the hydromorph will harass and try to prevent the players once they head towards the submarine dock with the battery (they sense the electricity).


Take command over the submersible

Installing the battery will require a successful heavy machinery test.

To properly start the submarine, a successful comtech test will be needed.

The ceiling of the underwater dock opens to let the Baikal exit to the sea through a specialized airlock that depends on one operator due to years of no maintenance. This person will be abandoned; if only one player is here, they can try to blow the hatch remotely, but this will damage the submersible!


The ascend

If the players manage to start the submarine and begin to ascend, the hydromorphs will try one last time to stop them, surrounding the submarine and attempting to drain the battery or damage the sub.

A successful piloting test will allow the submarine to escape, or a series of then, have fun GM.

In the SURFACE UMBILICAL

The xenos will cease to harass the submersible once it gains speed, but upon reaching the surface station, the players will be greeted by the presence of Gen. Volkoff and a whole capture team in specialized suits, along with elite soldiers, and will be promptly detained, their future uncertain in the hands of the General.

In the Korab Station

If the players decide to go to the Korab station, they will escape the General but be stranded in a remote location with no communications, no food, and with the possibility of the xenos to surface eventually, their future uncertain and dire.

Routine Maintenance Gone Wrong... Again.

 

(My friend here makes a awesome Frenkel! See you around Guilherme!)

 

(If someone is in the seabed with Frenkel, make him disappear into the dark before they can do something about it. This event is proof that something is in the water beyond any doubt.)

 

NPC Frenkel, suffering from the worst hangover, goes out to finish the maintenance Kirill never completed.

An alarm goes off, indicating Frenkel's hose has been disconnected (everyone adds one stress when the alarm sounds).

Frenkel screams over the communicator, gasping, scared, terrified. "Oh my God, what...", more sharp screams follow and then muffle, as Frenkel alternates between his main connection and his backup breathing device.

Heavy breaths are heard: "help me!", "something is here", "please!".

Frenkel cannot be seen visually as he is behind the drill and a camera that would normally cover him is no longer working.

A flash of light, a blur, a swirl of the sea is seen near the area if anyone bothers to look through the porthole.

Frenkel needs help, and the players need to act.

If no one volunteers to go out and rescue him, an NPC will immediately order them to rescue Frenkel.

 

The hydromorphs have disconnected Frenkel's air and are playing with him, probing and testing how the players react.

Frenkel will continue to scream over their communicators while the players prepare to go after him (more stress will be added at the GM's discretion once the players are in the air chamber).

When the players reach Frenkel, they will find him tangled in his own disconnected air hose, nearly out of air and injured.

Players must make a proper mobility check to untangle him.

Once they attempt to rescue Frenkel, the hydromorphs will attack using only option #2 on their characteristic attack table (dragging the players away, screaming, and then releasing them).

Some players' hoses will be disconnected by the hydromorphs, and the player will then need to switch to their secondary emergency air tank. This requires a mobility test.

Failure to secure the secondary breathing device will add +1 stress. Running out of air can result in damage and even death if not corrected (at the GM's discretion).

If the PCs manage to bring Frenkel back, he will be in shock and die shortly after, convulsing with wide eyes.

A medical examination will reveal lacerations and strange burn marks all over his torso as the hydromorphs drained his electrical life energy from his body.

Arrival

  • Arrival of the group

  • Time to argue, investigate the disappearance, assess the station's condition, and point fingers!

  • Strange noises and errors in the terminals.

  • Babushka wakes up and claims she saw the devil!

  • More time for blaming each other!

  •  

!!! Frenkel (Event) Disappears!!! There's a creature here!

 

  • Discover that the elevator has been disabled at the surface base.

    • The Captain of the Ship that transported Olga to Novotny will mechanically disable the surface elevator. If reviewed through camera recordings, the footage will reveal him following instructions displayed on a pad.

    • The captain appears unaware of the purpose or consequences of his actions—he is simply following orders without question.

 

!!! Determine how to escape (submarine, batteries at the old station, installation, etc.)!!!

 

  • It's evident that these creatures are not from here! Will they try to learn more about them?

  • Maria wants to drug the people (she could blame Dubois as the drug is a narcotic).

  • Babushka might try to go out to placate the devil!

  • The drill will break if not repaired, which may be seen as intentional destruction of government property. Will they go out to fix it?

 

!!! Reason to go to the crashed ship?  the fear of not being found if you disappear!!!

  

  • Can they hack 1/VAN and discover about Marill and the crashed ship? Will they go there?

  • During any walk, it is noticed that the locator's detection antenna is broken. Will they fix it?

    • If fixed, the locator will show that any missing person was taken to the ship.

    • Impregnation is impossible in the water, but the xenos had not understand that yet.


!!! At the Start of Ascension or Death (Final Act)!!!

 

!!! The creatures attack the station if they take too long to act, and begin to invade!!!

  • When a creature enters by breaching, water enters and the system tries to isolate that area.

    • The bulkhead system seals the initial breach (a hole in the hull is sealed by an emergency inflatable bulkhead, not with air, it's a gel that solidifies inside the inflatable), and now there's a xeno in the base...

 

  • When a creature enters by using any garbage shut, or other means, they may stay hidden, amazing to allow hydrohuggers in.

pages.name: Terminal message to Captain Kramarenko (show at the start)

text.content:
Drinking Too Much!

Frenkel, Diego, and Dubov spent the last night drinking and playing cards, celebrating that after six months of rotation, Diego was about to get a vacation—alongside Maria, who wasn't at the party.

Only Dubov’s legendary stamina held up the next day. Frenkel has a headache, and Diego overslept, now thinking he would miss the off-world transport.

He might first encounter Olga, running half-dressed in a panic about missing the elevator, only to learn that the captain had already arrived and the station was on lockdown.

Not the best way to start!

Li Qiang Fear

Li Qiang is terrified at the thought of being imprisoned for embezzlement and other financial crimes. He also fears the possibility that his corruption may have caused or contributed to Kirill's death. On top of this, he is certain that Volkov will either pin the blame or direct his wrath onto Li—and he doubts he will survive either outcome.

Li will do everything in his power to avoid taking the fall. He will destroy evidence, shift blame onto the crew, the UPP, or anything else that might serve his purpose.

He might even exploit the monster as a distraction to cover his tracks or eliminate anyone who could incriminate him. It will take him some time to realize that the creature poses a far greater threat than his crimes.

The Madness of Maria

Maria is suffering from hallucinations due to an uncommon side effect of having received her dose of Dekompress to prepare for her return to the surface at the end of her shift. She was scheduled to leave on the ship that brought Captain Olga, ending her six-month service rotation for some well-deserved rest.

Maria believes the monster isn’t real. When she sees it, she struggles to comprehend what it is, often dismissing or forgetting its existence altogether, even hallucination or conjuring another explanation.

She secretly plans to use the Dekompress Antidote on the crew. This prevents the recipient from adjusting to surface pressure (making any attempt to ascend fatal) but does not stop them from remaining at the current depth.

The antidote immediately reduces stress by half, induces sleep, and stops panic effects.

However, it causes recent memory loss, leaving the person unaware they were injected.

The drug also has narcotic properties, and Maria might shift blame onto Dubov for the disappearance of the stolen medication from MEDLAB. Conveniently, the medlab cameras have been broken for a long time, giving her cover for her actions.

Cautious Players

If the players are overly cautious about leaving the base, create a serious problem to push them into action.

In my sessions, I introduced a scenario where the base maintains part of its integrity using external artificial gravity generation plates. These plates are designed to reduce external pressure but consume significant energy—making them an attractive target for both Long Salmons and Hydromorphs.

If the plates are damaged, it can trigger a timed crisis that must be resolved before irreversible damage occurs! I usually target the hydroponics system, as its failure compromises air filtration and food production. However, it doesn’t block access to other sectors, ensuring the players still have options while dealing with the escalating threat.

It is Just a F**** FISH!!!!!

When Frenkel disappears or during the monster's first appearance to a diver, instead of immediately revealing the Hydromorph, use the the invisible Bioluminos TOKEN.



This will send the diver fleeing in panic back to the airlock. Once things seem more under control, surprise the group by having a Long Salmon token in the airlock.

As they investigate the incident, since life doesn't exist in VODA, they'll uncover ties to the abandoned Korab Station. SCADA’s system, still operational, holds information about past aquaculture experiments and secrets connected to the current events.

To deepen the mystery and horror, give the Long Salmon strange scars across its face.

—a beautiful baby Hydrobuster gestating inside the fish, ready to escalate the chaos.

Invasion

After some time, introduce the invasion of the base by the creatures.

Start with Hydrohuggers infiltrating through the debris ejection hatches. Their small size allows them to slip through unnoticed until it’s too late.

Soon after, Hydromorphs follow, escalating the threat. They can use the same debris hatches, but they cause damage, and alarms, or they can force their way through weakened sections of the base.

In response, the hull-sealing systems will activate automatically (hull sealing not watertight doors, yet), but they won’t be enough to fully stop the water.

Water will slowly begin to flood the base, players must deal with both the invading creatures and the encroaching flood.


Random location table


Test if you want a random location for a Hydromorph problem or any issue to occur. External locations will only have Hydromorphs if there is human presence.


@UUID[RollTable.VsCouCOzwuZZHD71]{Random location table}

Summary of the Story


General Volkov oversees a UPP sector that includes the VODA planet and the Novotny station on it. For years, he and his team, with the help of Li Qiang, the station supervisor, have embezzled funds for personal gain. Due to bureaucratic convenience, Li Qiang operates closely with Volkov's team instead of Voda.

The Ministry of Space Security (MSS) dispatched Captain Olga Kramarenko for a routine inspection and state audit of VODA. A renowned war hero with a reputation for being incorruptible, Olga represents a serious threat to Volkov's operations. To safeguard his interests, Volkov instructs Li Qiang to go with her, joining the ship during transit, though his apprehension remains palpable.

While Olga and Qiang are still en route, Volkov receives a report from Novotny station: the base's computer mentions Xenomorphs, followed hours later by a message from the crew about a missing, presumed-dead diver, this clear that the crew doesn’t know about the Xenomorphs.

 

Investigating, Volkov learns sparse details about the Xenomorphs. He devises a ruthless plan: use the creatures to eliminate witnesses, wipe out the crew, and capture the aliens for his own advantage within the UPP.

He instructs the transport ship's captain to perform "maintenance" on the station's elevator. Unaware of the implications, the captain disables the elevator, trapping the crew in the depths of the ocean.

At the station, the only escape option is an abandoned, unreliable submersible. From here, character agendas and interpersonal conflicts drive the story.

Acts Breakdown

  • Act 1 ends when it becomes clear to the crew that escape is their only option—monsters have appeared, and survival becomes the top priority.

  • There are no three distinct acts in this scenario.

pages.name: CIXIN LIU STATION ENGINEER  (UNOFFICIAL TEAM LEADER)

text.content:
CIXIN LIU - Chief Engineer

  • Full Name: Cixin Liu
  • Role: Station Engineer
  • Age: 52
  • Personality: Independent

Cixin Liu has worked at Novotny Station for over 25 years. He firmly believes that only through hard work and dedication can the people of the UPP advance their cause across the galaxy.

Proud of ensuring the station’s equipment operates correctly, Liu has faced increasing frustration as his repeated requests for basic tools are ignored. Despite these challenges, he has devoted his life to Novotny and dreams of restoring it to its former glory. However, this current shift under the sea has tested even his unyielding resolve.

He despises the station's hierarchical corruption and sees this investigation—and Olga’s arrival—as a chance to finally bring change.

Attributes

  • Strength: 3
  • Wits: 5
  • Empathy: 4
  • Agility: 2

Health: 3

Skills

  • Heavy Machinery: 5
  • Observation: 3
  • Comtech: 5
  • Command: 1

Talent: Analysis

Signature Item: Sci-Fi Story Novel
Equipment: Seegson Electronics Kit (+1 to Comtech)

Cpt. Olga Kramarenko

Occupation: MSS Agent
Age: 36
Personality: Direct

ATTRIBUTES

STRENGTH: 5
WITS: 3
EMPATHY: 3
AGILITY: 3

HEALTH: 5

SKILLS

  • Close Combat: 3
  • Ranged Combat: 3
  • Command: 4
  • Observation: 2

TALENTS

  • Pull Rank

Signature Item: Bravery Medal

EQUIPMENT

  • UPP 9mm Service Pistol (2 loads)
  • Large Serrated Underwater Combat Knife (DMG 2)
  • P-DAT

Backstory

Cpt. Olga Kramarenko once commanded an elite unit of underwater demolition commandos. Her unshakable loyalty to the UPP was severely tested about a year ago when her entire team was abandoned in enemy-infested waters. She emerged as the sole survivor.

Awarded a bravery medal for her actions, Olga found herself emboldened enough to question her superiors about the decisions that led to this military catastrophe. Their response was swift: she was "promoted" and reassigned to the Ministry of Space Security, ostensibly as a reward for her valor, but in reality, it was a means of sidelining her.

Her next assignment took her to the aquatic world of Voda, tasked with investigating a series of disappearances. Cautious but dutiful, Olga prepared for the mission, knowing full well she couldn't trust the motives of her superiors.

Ivan Dubov

Occupation: Machine Operator
Age: 25
Personality: Rebellious

ATTRIBUTES

STRENGTH: 5
WITS: 2
EMPATHY: 2
AGILITY: 5

HEALTH: 5

SKILLS

  • Heavy Machinery: 4
  • Close Combat: 3
  • Manipulation: 1
  • Ranged Combat: 2

TALENTS

  • The Long Haul

Signature Item: Cigarette Case

EQUIPMENT

  • Razor-Sharp Switchblade (DMG 2)

Backstory

Ivan Dubov is an underwater welder specializing in deep-sea operations. Once a free spirit, his penchant for illegal gambling repeatedly brought him into conflict with the state. He was eventually sentenced to forced labor.

After spending several years in a labor prison, Ivan was given a choice: continue his grueling sentence or sign a decades-long contract to work on the underwater station. He reluctantly chose the latter.

A recent arrival at the station, Ivan has proven to be a thorn in the side of seasoned workers like Liu, whom he constantly antagonizes. His rebellious attitude and disciplinary issues have led to him being barred from joining the other workers on most tasks, relegating him to menial jobs like cleaning latrines in the habitation area.

Though outwardly defiant, Ivan dreams of escaping what he sees as a life of slavery and charting his own course. He only trusts a few people, and most of the station’s staff are not on that list.

pages.name: KIM PHAM - ESPECIALISTA EM MERGULHO / MÉDICO

text.content:
Kim Pham

Occupation: Diving Specialist / Medic
Age: 28
Personality: Curious



ATTRIBUTES

STRENGTH: 3
WITS: 4
EMPATHY: 5
AGILITY: 2

HEALTH: 3



SKILLS

  • Observation: 3
  • Comtech: 3
  • Medical Aid: 4



TALENTS

  • Field Surgeon

Signature Item: Old Family Photo



EQUIPMENT

  • Personal Med Kit
  • AMVIL'S HEART! (Naproleve -UPP) (2 doses)



Backstory

Dr. Kim Pham grew up in a farming cooperative far from the ocean, dreaming of exploring alien worlds and charting new frontiers. A trailblazer in her family, she became the first to receive formal education, choosing a career in medicine.

Driven by her passion for discovery, she seized the opportunity to work on an underwater station on a distant alien planet, acing every underwater skills test with perfect scores.

However, shortly after her arrival at Matvey Station, Pham learned that her family had perished in a devastating—yet preventable—farming accident. This tragedy shattered her trust in the UPP’s promises to care for its citizens, leaving her disillusioned and burdened with regret over her decision to join.

Despite her internal conflict, Pham remains a skilled and compassionate medic, committed to helping those in her care.

Diego Alvarez

Occupation: UPP State Agent
Age: 31
Personality: Optimistic

ATTRIBUTES

STRENGTH: 3
WITS: 5
EMPATHY: 3
AGILITY: 3

HEALTH: 3

SKILLS

  • Close Combat: 2
  • Observation: 2
  • Survival: 1
  • Comtech: 4
  • Ranged Combat: 1

TALENTS

  • Cunning

Signature Item: UPP Shoulder Patch

EQUIPMENT

  • Custom Underwater Power Tool (DMG 2)

Backstory

Born on an aquatic world plagued by scarcity and hardship, Diego Alvarez grew up in a community where survival was a daily struggle. Recognized for his aptitude in science, he earned a spot in a UPP state cooperative, specializing in underwater mining and serving as a company representative.

Despite his corporate role, Diego is not the stereotypical company agent. His actions are guided by compassion and humanism rather than ambition or ruthlessness. His optimistic outlook and genuine desire to help others set him apart from his peers.

Recently assigned to Matvey Station as part of an interplanetary exchange program, Diego enjoyed a carefree evening of drinking and card games with Dubov and Frenkel. Unfortunately, he overslept, missing the scheduled elevator departure to the surface. He awakens to find the station in lockdown and chaos unfolding around him.
This list is designed for the players, keeping any hidden agendas and secret information out of sight, allowing them to choose their characters freely.

The central corridor doubles as an exercise area for the facility's personnel. Embedded in its inner wall is a massive emergency pump.

The red switch used to activate the pump (in case of catastrophic flooding) is housed within a glass enclosure that requires a Strength test with a heavy object or tool to break.

The identical switch in the control room is no longer functional, though no one is aware of this.

Both the supervisor @UUID[Actor.4GcdxJq9BPDZ1BAN]{LI QIANG} and the engineer @UUID[Actor.XXpcnLOEf5YfefeR]{CIXIN LIU} possess keys to unlock the glass case.

Activating the pump can drain a flooded sealed room or slow down flooding. If used in emergency mode, it will seal all watertight doors.

The living quarters are a large area with bunks that accommodate all the station workers. Each bunk has personal lockers for the occupants. There are also several latrines, shower rooms, and laundry machines.

Mess hall

All station workers gather here for their meals several times a day. Meals are served by Working Joe NS42 ("Dmitri," see background details), a permanently assigned Working Joe for this station.

Coffee and occasional snacks are available, though snacks have been almost nonexistent for several months now.

Some tables have been repurposed into card and domino tables.

In one corner, there’s an old but functioning arcade machine featuring Tetris, and in another, a homemade vodka distillery.

While both are against protocol (especially the arcade machine), no one seems to mind these added amenities.

Dmitri enjoys the arcade machine and is surprisingly skilled at it.

Landing Platform

Spanning nearly 150 meters in length and in relatively good condition, the landing platform—like the rest of the surface support—rests on a semi-submerged structure. It is stabilized by mechanical systems, mooring lines, and, in emergencies, auxiliary motors.

Though neglected in terms of cleanliness and paint maintenance, the platform remains structurally sound and secure.

The helipad houses an ancient helicopter, over 100 years old, once used to access another base.

No one remembers why it exists here, but records can be found.

The vehicle is in a state of complete disrepair, far beyond any hope of restoration.

Connecting Corridor

A corridor links the landing platform to the surface base. Access is managed by a Working Joe NS42 unit, which grants entry authorization.
Security, access and communication can be done here.
Access to the almost empty deposit, nothing really useful here

Diving Suits

Diving suit storage, waiting for divers to descend via the open elevator.

Armor 4

If the armor value is reduced to zero and the victim is in the water, they die instantly as the crushing pressure tears through the suit like a bag of chips...

Base Hose Connection

If open the victim cannot breathe, but a feedback valve prevents water from directly entering the suit. It takes a Fast Action and a MOBILITY test at -2 to grab the loose hose. A HEAVY MACHINERY test is required to reconnect the hose.

Emergency Air

It takes a Slow Action and a successful HEAVY MACHINERY test to equip the emergency air supply.

Drowning:

If the user cannot breathe (i.e., no air supply), they must make a DROWNING test (STAMINA) at the start of their action - if failed, they take 1 point of damage. If broken by this method, they must make a DEATH SAVE or depart this mortal coil!

pg 110 core rule book

Elevator

The elevator is a steel container guided by cables, designed to transport personnel to the submerged base. It is exposed to water, making the use of diving suits essential for descent.

For this scenario, the elevator cannot be used to return to the surface.

It was disabled immediately after the team's descent by the captain of the Schatzi, acting under orders and threats from General Volkoff.

Restoring its functionality is not possible unless the GM decides to conclude the scenario differently.
DEKOMPRESS MEDS

These rooms are filled with monitors displaying external footage of the station. They also have replay capabilities and can store up to a month of data.

The rooms are equipped with general alarm monitors as well.

If someone decides to review past video logs, they may notice strange anomalies—shadows, energy blurs, and bizarre lights outside the station—coinciding with recent equipment malfunctions over the past few days.

Monitoring Stations

These rooms are filled with monitors displaying external footage of the station. They also feature replay capabilities and can store up to one month of data.

The rooms also include monitors for general alarms.

If someone reviews past video recordings, they may find unusual anomalies—shadows, energy distortions, and bizarre lights outside the station—coinciding with strange equipment malfunctions in recent days.

Command Center

All drilling operations are managed from this area. Monitoring sensors, chemical equipment, controls, and monitors fill the room.

A glass dome at the ceiling offers unobstructed views of one side of the drilling system and most of the station. However, the exterior of the dome is significantly dirtied, obscuring visibility.

SCADA Computer Access

Capable of reading computer accesses, interacting, and commanding, but not examining the mainframe hardware, just a remote dedicated terminal to SCADA..



@UUID[.nwndPSWdvflWlgbL]{SCADA CPU}

SCADA - 1/VAN

Previously known as 1/VAN, now referred to as SCADA (Supervision Control And Data Acquisition), this system has suffered significant command corruption.

SCADA operates as a standard monitoring and data acquisition system in all respects except one: when a Xenomorphic presence is detected. In such instances, it activates its only remaining functional commands:

  • B000108: Alert the UPP of the detection.
  • A001107: Dispatch an agent to investigate under strict secrecy.

Other commands are visible to users but are incomplete and are ignored by SCADA - 1/VAN.

SCADA retains access to @UUID[Actor.Pv8jNWHyxSi59K0A]{Working Joe NS42 “Dmitri”} and any other synthetics on the station.

However, 1/VAN itself does not, leaving it unable to defend itself effectively. This creates a scenario akin to a split personality, with neither side fully aware of the other.

Background
1/VAN is an old AI system recycled from Ouragan Station 15 years ago (an OLD 1/VAN 3).

Hydroponics

Work shifts on the station can last up to a year or even longer under certain circumstances. Therefore, the station's ability to grow its own food is critical.

All kinds of vegetables, proteins, and fruits are cultivated here.

The hydroponics area is maintained by @UUID[Actor.GjObv8jhwRpwB7jZ]{Maria Del Campos} and @UUID[Actor.12vb86KU6IWdlPGj]{Joe NS42 "BORIS"} (Roughneck).

Filtration Systems

The air recyclers and water filtration systems are located in this area and are accessible via a small circular hatch. A failure in these systems could eventually necessitate the evacuation of all station workers.

The monitoring station equipped with lights and switches oversees these systems.

The purge station can cleanse the air of any contaminants, but it renders the environment unbreathable within 15 minutes. The purge process lasts for 2 hours, requiring the use of breathing apparatus during this time.

GM Note:


This location is crucial due to its control over the station's air supply. If your players are too cautious or hesitant, consider putting this area in jeopardy! A malfunction, sabotage, or sudden contamination could force them to act quickly, creating tension and urgency in their decision-making

Power Loader

A deactivated and irrecoverable power loader, abandoned here after the reactor was activated. The battery still works, but the environment is radioactive.

Radiation - pg 110, ALIEN CRB Strong Radiation: 1 Rad per Turn

Removing battery: 4 turns heavy machinery test.

This battery is not completely compatible with the submersible, another 2 turns and a Heavy Machinery Test is required to adapt.
Permanent block compatible with expansion modules that never arrived

Storage

Every conceivable piece of old equipment can be found in this area, some literally a century old.

Older pressure suits, some still functioning, and antique fishing harpoons that were never useful in this sea.

You'll see submarine equipment of all kinds, emergency lights, flares, and old respiratory devices. There are also old data blocks, newspapers, and magazines detailing the station's glory days, along with dusty files and records.

Among the clutter, you'll find spent batteries, a portrait of a former UPP leader, an employee of the year plaque, a Siberian teddy bear, and a 357 Rivet Bang Stick typically used for aggressive aquatic life converted to riveting, which has 6 charges.

GM!


A shelf of documents that, on their own, do not prove corruption but provide hints. These suggest that the rest of the archive in the hangar contains the answers, holding all sorts of proof of corruption for those who seek it. The documents are moved to the hangar after being sealed in waterproof boxes to free up space.

Li Qiang will try to burn this documents if he starts to believe he will be caught.

Maintenance

All machinery necessary for external maintenance activities is here, as well as all the equipment for repairs when done at the submerged base.

A large screen can monitor any camera in real-time, including helmet cameras, used for mechanics to observe defects before making decisions. many external cameras are broken or dirty lenses.

This room is responsible for locally monitoring the dives and the external situation of the base, including the drilling rig, life support monitors, air pumps, and all necessary support for external tasks.

DEKOMPRESS MEDS Cabinets


@UUID[.duXumfw0nJhhvF0B]{DEKOMPRESS Syringes}

The area features built-in wall cabinets. These cabinets hold deep-sea diving equipment such as suits, helmets, emergency respirators, and harpoons used to anchor equipment to the seabed.

Benches line the walls and are used to prepare divers for sea walks (see Sea Walks).

Additionally, emergency air kits (15 minutes) and long-walk air kits (6 hours) are stored here.

Medical Bay

At the start of the scenario, one worker has fallen ill. Anya Zomorova is under the care of Dr. Kim Pham. She is connected to a machine after being severely debilitated during her search for the missing worker. She was awaiting evacuation when the order to remain below came from above (see story points).

The facility includes two rooms with beds for more intensive care and one room with multiple practical medical stations designed for quick assessments and treatments.

The medical bay, while not state-of-the-art and lacking medical capsule technology, is equipped with standard tools for examination and emergency stabilization. The bay is attended by Joe NS42.

Dr. Pham has access to limited medications, six medkits, and a large stock of DEKOMPRESS, but the antidote for this medication has mysteriously gone missing.

Air Lock

The station has three airlocks serving as access points to the external environment. One at the elevator, one in Heavy Works and One in the Hangar


(The Old Station utilizes a vertical stairwell , equipped with two watertight doors as an airlock to transition between the station and the external environment, its manual and 2 divers can use the space between doors during transitions.

Additionally, the flooded tunnel can function as an airlock as well to the hangar, utilizing its two watertight doors in the same manner.)

They function as follows:

Divers enter the airlock and seal the bulkhead door when ready to transition to the seafloor. A large internal metal key initiates the process (a manual override located outside the bulkhead door can also start this process).

A red light illuminates, and over the course of 60 seconds, the chamber fills with external water. Once the process is complete, the chamber equalizes, and a green light signals that it is now safe to exit the station.

The metal doors to the exterior retract when another lever is operated.

(See the section on Sea Walks for more

information.@UUID[JournalEntry.2A70WlvyYoIRKyer.JournalEntryPage.sBcSRhMYrnBozOh8]{Sea Walks}

This corridor suffered a catastrophic failure years ago. Never repaired, its entrances were sealed by the automatic system and the Hangar largely abandoned. The access to the Jogging was also welded shut from the inside.



Access to the hangar is functional, BUT IT REQUIRES AN EXTERNAL BATTERY TO OPEN!!

WITH THE BATTERY - HEAVY MACHINERY TEST, 1 TURN

WITHOUT THE BATTERY - HEAVY MACHINERY TEST -3, 3 TURNSS

!!!! THE BREATHING HOSES DO NOT GO THROUGH THE CORRIDOR MORE THAN A FEW METERS WITHOUT CONSTANTLY GETTING ENTANGLED (MOBILITY TEST), AND THEY MUST BE LEFT BEHIND!!

Drill Platform

For over 100 years, the drill platform has been extracting oil from the ocean floor. Its systems are entirely submerged, with no dry areas available. The operation is autonomous, theoretically requiring only periodic maintenance.

Significant Events

  • Kirill’s Disappearance: It was on this platform that Marin Kirill reportedly vanished.

  • Frenkell’s Attack: The platform becomes the site of a pivotal event when Frenkell is attacked. The players may witness or investigate the aftermath, adding tension and urgency to their mission.

Underwater HANGAR Dock

This is the permanent home of the Baikal, a deep-sea submersible.

The vessel is a spherical design built to accommodate up to three individuals (GM discretion).

Originally created for deep-sea research, it played a vital role in the final phase of construction and expansion of the Novotny station. Now inactive, it serves as a potential escape vessel in emergencies.

The Baikal has not been used for decades. It relies on three old, large solid batteries, which were disconnected and moved to the old station for other projects. A single battery is sufficient to power the sub to the surface.

The underwater dock's ceiling opens to release the Baikal into the sea through a specialized airlock. This system relies on cranes to move the submersible into position.

  • Manual Operation Required: The system functions but requires an operator to ensure safe operation. Without an operator, the submersible will sustain damage and lose one piloting point. The operator must stay behind, sacrificing themselves.

  • System Restart: The system must be reactivated before use.

    • CONTECH Test: To restart the system properly.
    • Heavy Machinery Test (-2): For a risky direct WIRING.

  • No Initial Power: The dock has no power before reactivation.

    • Attempting to force the lights on using a battery will render the battery unusable. A CONTECH Test is required to understand this risk.

Underwater Dock

This area houses the Baikal, a deep-sea submersible.

  • Design and Capacity:
    The Baikal is a spherical vessel designed for a crew of up to three (GM discretion). Originally intended for deep-sea research, it played a crucial role in the final construction phase and expansion of the Novotny station. Today, it serves as a last-resort escape craft in emergencies.

  • Current Status:
    The Baikal hasn’t been operational for decades. Its power source, three solid-state batteries, was repurposed for other projects. Only one battery retains a charge and could power the Baikal to the surface.

Airlock and Crane System

The dock’s ceiling airlock is designed to release the submersible into the ocean, guided by a system of cranes.

  • Operator Required: Due to years of neglect, the system requires an operator to ensure safe operation. Without one, the submersible will sustain damage, losing 1 point of piloting capability. The operator, however, must stay behind, making this a potential sacrificial act.

Power Restoration

  • Reactivation Steps:
    The system must be reconnected via a CONTECH Test or a -2 Heavy Machinery roll for a direct but risky bypass.

  • Critical Warning:
    Power is unavailable until the system is restored (TERMINAL IN THE UPPER RIGHT). Attempting to force the lights using the single battery will render the battery unusable. A CONTECH Test reveals this risk before action.

Pile of Old Bureaucratic Files and Office Discards

For years, an administrative order dictated that files must be sent digitally, final digital and physical records stored in the archive.

However, these documents were, by law, never to be discarded, and over time, the growing pile of files became a storage issue.

In an attempt to free up space without committing the crime of document disposal, the files were gradually moved to the abandoned hangar, creating a de facto dead archive.

Annual Transfer

Once a year, with the connecting corridor out of service, a task force transports sealed boxes of that year’s documents to the hangar. Despite the laborious journey, this is seen as a better option than risking a gulag sentence for destroying documents.

This is a chaotic graveyard of forgotten bureaucracy, neglect, outdated systems, and the desperate lengths people go to in order to avoid harsh consequences.

Evidence of Corruption

But all the evidence of corruption by Li Qiang, General Volkov and others is here!

There are clear signs of tools being used to force an opening through a damaged section of the tail.

This was undoubtedly done while the ship was still in vacuum—it was boarded in space!

Inside the wreckage, the body of the missing operator Marin Kirill is found, crushed by the pressure when their suit failed.

There are five large fish still alive, trapped against the walls in resin, with evidence of at least ten more dead.

Strange eggs are scattered throughout the ship, but they appear to be deliberately organized. One of them seems to contain a fish slowly transforming into a larger egg.

Additionally:

  • A damaged terminal is present. It can be salvaged and repaired back at the base to extract information.
  • Cryotubes containing a strange bioforms are part of the cargo.
  • --- An Egg and an Drone are still in cryochambers, other cryos are destroyed
  • An investigation reveals the remains of pilots wearing UPP commando suits, with two bodies restrained and executed in a corner, clear evidence of forced boarding.
  • While the ship was hijacked by the UPP, the cargo displays unmistakable signs of being UA in origin.

Some information, specifically medical forensics are quite hard, apply any penalties, but I like to share this discoveries freely, after all, they will probably die, either by the nest or by the angry Hydromorphs that will defend the nest.

The cargo is linked to something labeled "Life Force Program."

The Access room has a locked gate, but only leads to the nearly empty storage. A few chairs and a table adorn the sparse area.

A giant portrait of Pietro Novotny on the far wall greets all visitors and workers. Aside from the image of the current UPP leader, it is the only relatively new item in the room.

A small dilapidated medical area

The only true useful item are the dekompress.



DEKOMPRESS Syringes


DEKOMPRESS syringes can be found in all dive preparation areas, medkits, and medbays. The drug prevents the effects of decompression sickness if taken up to an hour before diving and the same before returning to the surface. Failing to do so means death at such deeps. 

Since there are no decompression chambers available, these syringes are essential for anyone attempting to leave Novotny without succumbing to this potentially fatal condition.

Elevator Monitoring

Monitors are installed to ensure the elevator's safety and proper operation. These systems provide real-time data on its status and performance.

The red switch used to activate the pump (in case of catastrophic flooding) is housed within a glass enclosure, requiring a Strength test with a heavy object or tool to break.

The corresponding switch in the control room is no longer functional, a fact that remains unknown to the crew.

Supervisor @UUID[Actor.4GcdxJq9BPDZ1BAN]{LI QIANG} and engineer @UUID[Actor.XXpcnLOEf5YfefeR]{CIXIN LIU} each hold a key to unlock the glass case.

Activating the pump can drain a sealed flooded room or slow the progression of a flood. When used in emergency mode, it will automatically seal all watertight doors.

This is the century-old remnant of the original station, used as a construction base before the expansion of the main facility.

  • External Hatch: Opening the external hatch requires a STRENGTH Test.

Upon entering and removing underwater gear, players will be overwhelmed by the pervasive stench of brine and crude oil.

Batteries

The three solid-state batteries that could power the Baikal have been repurposed to run an oil analyzer unit.

  • Battery Status:

    • Only one battery still holds a charge, as it remains connected to the analyzer, which recharges itself using residual energy from the nuclear core.
    • The other two batteries are depleted and will require recharging before use if that is intended.

This location can serve as a pivotal challenge, forcing players to strategize carefully about how to retrieve and use the last functional battery.

About Deep Down

After running the Colonial Marines campaign—which my players absolutely loved—despite having zero prior experience with the Alien RPG, I decided to take on a cinematic scenario. I was already set on using Dead Sea, but my players were eager to face the Xenos, so I made some adjustments!

It was a blast! I've run it several times now, receiving great feedback, so I decided to share it!

Now I'm making a joke with the directions. First, DEEP DOWN, and now they're playing CRAWLING UP!—a mini-campaign on its 8 sessions and not even half way. Next will be RUNNI... oops, they don't know that yet! 😉
